- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% to match mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to align with sentiment cooling.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.4) and model forecast is flat or falling, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to match sentiment trend.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term volatility in 30-day horizon; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce noise in forecast tails.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.1–0.3) and price is near recent 10-day mean, model often drifts toward extreme values; anchor forecast to 10-day moving average with ±1.5% buffer.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and model forecast is above 70, model tends to overestimate recovery; cap forecast at 70–72 unless sentiment rebounds sharply.
